coupling_sign_mutation.mirror_symmetry_note: While the 1D Pierce cubic is mirror-symmetric under (b, sign_cpl) -> (-b, -sign_cpl) (x1(+1,+1) = x1(-1,-1) = 0.6891 and x1(-1,+1) = x1(+1,-1) = 0.3066), in the 22-period 2D FIT run (m in [8, 19]) only the peak moves from +b to -b: the peak pair gives alpha(+b,+1) = 202.42 Np/m vs alpha(-b,-1) = 215.09 Np/m (6.26% difference), whereas mirror symmetry FAILS on the off-peak pair: alpha(-b,+1) = 29.33 Np/m vs alpha(+b,-1) = 178.41 Np/m (508.2% difference). This asymmetry is not predicted by the 3-wave Pierce BVP, which is exactly mirror-symmetric at all z; it is unexplained. (The live 10-period test at 0.45 A, m in [5, 8], is a different current and window.)

current_cube_root_scaling.deembedding_note: The raw 22-period FIT window slope over m in [8, 19] (18.75, 64.73, 145.92, 236.49 Np/m) does NOT follow I0^(1/3): its log-log slope is 1.4575 because low-current runs (I0 = 0.08 A, CN ~ 0.15) remain inside the 3-wave launching dip across m in [8, 19]. The de-embedded rate alpha_fit_np_m (159.40, 197.06, 241.55, 292.71 Np/m, log-log slope 0.35166) is obtained by inverting Pierce's 3-wave BVP at period m = 19 using Pierce's own b = 0 and QC(I0), and lies 28.6%-33.3% (mean 31.6%) above the 1D Pierce prediction (123.97, 149.40, 181.25, 220.48 Np/m) at every current.

velocity_detuning_b.finite_cn_note: Relative difference vs the asymptotic single-wave Pierce rate is 6.93% at b = 0; 20.48% at b = -0.5 (not agreement); and 54.96% at b = -1.0 (29.33 vs 65.12 Np/m). At positive detuning b in {+0.7, +1.4, +2.2}, the 22-period FIT window slope (193.90, 203.71, 174.02 Np/m) exceeds the single-wave Pierce asymptote (146.74, 126.05, -0.00 Np/m). The 1D finite-window total-field BVP / crestatron model is WITHDRAWN as a quantitative explanation of the sweep because at b in {-1.0, -0.5, 0.0} it predicts -142.01, -266.46, and +15.74 Np/m versus the 2D FIT window slopes +29.33, +88.29, and +145.92 Np/m.

space_charge_qc_reduction.disagreement_explanation: At fixed b = 0, the infinite-length single-wave Pierce root x1(0, QC) cuts off to zero above QC_crit = 3/2^(8/3) = 0.4725 because the slow space-charge wave shifts to b_sync = sqrt(4 QC) > 1.37. Over the short 22-period FIT window (CN in [0.12, 0.30]), the uncalibrated on-axis slope decreases monotonically with QC (178.39 -> 145.92 -> 103.30 -> 66.23 Np/m) but remains positive at QC = 0.45 and 0.81 (103.30 and 66.23 Np/m vs Pierce 34.48 and 0.00 Np/m) because the 22-period window measures the total on-axis field including two-wave plasma beating and the local electrostatic space-charge field E_sc on-axis.
